newsitem.title: UK: CalEnergy raises stake in Northern Electric.
newsitem.headline: CalEnergy raises stake in Northern Electric.

text.p: U.S. group CalEnergy Co Inc's CE Electric UK unit said on Wednesday it raised its stake in Northern Electric Plc to 13.4 percent as part of its hostile bid for the British regional utility.

The unit bought 698,846 ordinary shares at the bid price of 630p per share, raising its total holding to about 13.6 million shares, according to a disclosure made to the London Stock Exchange by Hoare Govett Corporate Finance. On Monday, the company said it had a 12.7 percent stake in Northern Electric, which rejected CE Electric's estimated $1.2 billion bid but indicated it might consider a higher price.
Northern Electric slid 2.5p to 637 in morning trade.
CE Electric is 70 percent owned by Nebraska-based CalEnergy, with the remaining stake held by U.S. construction, mining and telecoms group Peter Kiewit Sons.
The company's bid marked the second unwanted advance for Northern Electric in two years.
